title: auth: clarify header semantics for project/org keys, scoped tokens, CORS, and request signing (OpenAI compat)
author: Asha Patel
description: Problem: Our OpenAI-compat layer and native API had diverging expectations for authentication headers: project-level keys (Project-Key), org-level keys (Authorization: Bearer org_...), scoped tokens for fine-grained permissions, CORS preflight behavior, and optional request signing/nonce headers used by private deployments. This caused inconsistent failure modes in browser clients and proxy setups. Motivation: unify semantics so SDKs and third-party users can rely on a single header contract across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments and preserve backward compatibility with OpenAI-compatible usage. Changes in this PR: 1) Canonical header precedence documented and implemented: Authorization: Bearer <token> (scoped tokens preferred) -> X-Project-Key for project-scoped keys -> X-Org-Key (deprecated but supported) ; 2) Introduce support for scoped token audience claim check (aud=redwood:api) and optional scope header X-Scopes for backwards introspection; 3) CORS: Add Access-Control-Expose-Headers for Authorization and X-Request-Nonce, ensure preflight allows X-Project-Key/X-Scopes/X-Request-Signature; 4) Request signing: accept X-Request-Signature and X-Request-Nonce for private deployments; signature check is opt-in via deployment config and off by default for hosted; 5) OpenAI-compat handler changes: compatibility shim accepts Authorization and Project-Key headers and maps them to internal identity; expands tests for streaming endpoints to assert header propagation; 6) SDK/quickstart updates: examples in TS/py showing browser-friendly patterns and how to use short-lived scoped tokens. Migration notes: existing tokens continue to work; org keys via X-Org-Key should migrate to Authorization but remain supported for 90 days with warning header. Rolling plan: feature-flagged on main, enable in staging for a week, then flip in prod. Checklist: - [x] Implement server-side parsing and precedence - [x] Add unit + integration tests (auth e2e) - [x] Add CORS exposure headers - [x] Update OpenAI-compat mappings - [x] Update SDK examples and docs - [x] Add migration warning header to deprecated X-Org-Key

release_notes: This change clarifies and unifies authentication header semantics across the Redwood API and OpenAI-compat layer. Highlights: 1) Canonical header precedence between Authorization, X-Project-Key, and X-Org-Key; 2) Scoped token audience checks and examples for short-lived browser tokens; 3) CORS preflight/exposed headers adjusted to allow browser clients to read auth-related headers; 4) Optional request signing (X-Request-Signature/X-Request-Nonce) for private deployments. Backwards compatible: X-Org-Key is deprecated but supported for a transitional period.
notes: Deployed behind feature flag. Staged rollout: staging -> canary prod -> global. Monitoring added: auth.header_errors, auth.signature_failures, openai_compat.header_warnings.
